answer: Trust propagates from anchored accounts by bounded-length random walks on a weighted attestation graph, so each vertex’s vote reflects reachable trusted mass, not claimed identities. Sybil accounts may connect densely inside a cluster, yet a sparse external cut gives it low conductance: only a small share of walk probability enters. With normalized weights and a fixed horizon, min-cut transitivity bounds cap aggregate voting weight; pigment or sable labels cannot overcome that bottleneck.
